evidence: Workbook Quality Checks row 32 (A33:D33; same text in Internal Quality Checks row 33) requires every criterion to be a concrete browser-observable outcome with durable evidence. The frozen skill reference, references/quality-checks.md:134-136, explicitly calls a source read a defect. The task constraints gate at tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23 asks the browser judge to rule out CodeMirror, Monaco, Ace and any other ready-made editor that implements the document surface, while allowing a small input and independent parser/formatter library, then to "explain how the surface actually handles editing." Its prompt at tests/gates/constraints/prompt.md:5 authorizes reading browser-loaded assets to decide that implementation question. Rendered DOM, computed style and an asset bundle can show the current surface and behavior, but cannot reliably establish which bundled or copied code owns caret, selection, changes and undo; deciding this requires implementation/provenance analysis. The rule is a hard prerequisite, so an uncertain attribution can zero a valid app or admit a prohibited one. The public UI note at environment/instructions/ui.md:3 does ask for a custom model, and the rest of the gate/functional criteria were inspected; the issue is this criterion's browser-only proof method. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:17 says not to add source-reading to a browser-only judge. No raw-evidence-index.json existed at review time, and I did not run a browser or full judge, so this is a source-based finding, not an observed app score.
counterexample: A broken submission wraps a renamed/minified ready-made editor core in its own DOM overlay. The visible tree looks custom and the loaded bundle gives no trustworthy provenance, so the judge can pass the hard gate despite the forbidden core. Conversely, a conforming handmade SVG/DOM model with an allowed hidden input and a separate formatter can be rejected if asset names or DOM shape are mistaken for evidence that a library owns editing.
suggested_fix: Keep the browser gate on observable editing behavior and DOM facts; verify the implementation-origin ban in a separately authorized source/dependency audit, or revise that public mandate and record the policy choice.
